# ACE/TAO C++17 modernization ledger

Scope: the complete ACE/TAO tree, including TAO_IDL, IFR_Service, tests,
examples, tools, and directories deferred in earlier passes. Continue using
one directory per batch, bundling the agreed modernization items for that
directory and recording validation here.

For directory/project counts and current per-directory status, see
[`modernization-status.md`](modernization-status.md) and
[`modernization-inventory.tsv`](modernization-inventory.tsv). This ledger is
the detailed history; an entry records work performed but does not imply that
the directory has had a complete audit against every modernization category.

## Follow-up tasks

- Across every directory and modernization pass in the complete ACE/TAO tree,
  remove standalone comments that add no information and only label a
  constructor, destructor, copy/move operation, or similar special member
  (for example, `//constructor`, `// constructor`, or `// destructor`). This
  applies to directories already modernized and code changed in earlier
  batches. Check generator inputs too, so label-only comments are not emitted
  into generated code. Retain comments that explain behavior, ownership, or
  non-obvious intent.

- For every directory in the complete ACE/TAO tree, review whether local
  variables can be declared in a narrower block or at the point of use.
  Apply scope reduction in the current modernization pass rather than
  waiting for Codacy findings; keep declarations broad only when later
  control flow needs them. Include previously modernized directories.

  client was separately compiled and linked with the same C++17 warning flags;
  no compiler warnings were emitted. `git diff --check`, 120-column, and
  repeated-blank checks passed.

must not be added to modernization commits.  Update it after every pushed
batch, and read the relevant directory entry before starting another sweep.

## Status key

- `initial pass complete`: The listed directory has received the agreed
  modernization review.  A later pass may still add a newly requested cleanup.
- `partial`: Only the named subdirectories or interface family have been
  completed.  Do not infer that sibling code was reviewed.
- `generated`: Do not edit directly; change the generator and validate output.

## Common completed tasks

Unless an entry narrows the scope, an initial pass covers safe C++17 changes:

- `override` only after verifying the immediate base and conditional variants.
- `= default` for empty special members and `= delete` for unwanted copying
  and moving, keeping declarations on one line.
- `explicit` for verified single-argument constructors that are not intended
  to support implicit conversion; preserve established var/out and conversion
  wrapper semantics.
- Internal `typedef` to `using`, pointer `0`/`NULL` to `nullptr`, and local
  scalar constants to `constexpr` where linkage/ODR use is safe.
- East-side `const`, without altering public ABI or generated/imported files.

1. Read this ledger and use `git log --grep='Modernize' -- <directory>` for
   the detailed prior change set.
2. Inspect only handwritten code; treat IDL-generated C/S/A files and export
   headers as generated unless their generator is the task.
3. Work in coherent directory or direct-interface-family batches, not one
   class per commit.
4. Start every rebuild with `make realclean`, regenerate MPC files when the
   target/project file requires it, and use `make -j 8`.
5. Update this ledger with the commit, scope, and exact validation result
   before moving to another directory.
6. Review changed classes for missing `override` specifiers and member
   functions that can be `const`; make these checks part of each modernization
   batch.

Review note: `TAO/TAO_IDL`'s `std::optional<UTL_StrList>` state in `IDL_GlobalData` is intentional. An absent list means template reference/alias context is inactive, while a present list supplies argument mapping; it is saved/restored across nested visitor traversal. Do not replace these optionals with empty vectors without redesigning the context state.

- `rhel101_acetao_debug_jwi/2026_11_08_12_01.txt` was built from fork commit
  `9b8cbde215f7`, before commit `ebd31d3b16a` updated the PortableGroup UIPMC
  wait-strategy constructors to use `unique_ptr::reset`. The two UIPMC compile
  errors in that log are stale against the current branch; subsequent missing
  `libTAO_PortableGroup` link errors are downstream. PortableGroup was later
  rebuilt locally after `realclean` and linked successfully. Do not add RHEL 8
  compatibility changes.

  in generated `Monitor::DataValue` sequence copying. Rebuilt the ACE core
  after `realclean`, then realclean-built and linked `TAO_Monitor`; that build
  emitted no warnings from the changed code.

## 2026-11-10 `IFR_Self_Recursive_IDL_Test` IOR output fix

- A focused runtime reproduction showed `server.ior` was created but empty:
  the scoped `FILE` owner survived into the blocking `orb->run()` call. Limited
  the owner lifetime to the IOR write block so close/flush happens before the
  event loop. After project regeneration, `make realclean`, `make -j 8`, and
  `perl run_test.pl` all succeeded.

## 2026-11-10 `Notify/performance-tests/Filter` IOR output fix

- The structured and sequence suppliers kept their IOR output files open while
  waiting for consumers. The harness waits for those IORs before launching a
  consumer, so the files remained empty and startup timed out. Scoped each
  unique file owner around the write so close/flush occurs immediately.
- Regenerated `Filter.mpc`; `make realclean` and `make -j 8` succeeded. The
  complete `perl run_test.pl` passed all four structured/sequence and filtered
  scenarios. `git diff --check` passed.
- A later Linux CI failure hit the default 20-second wait for the supplier IOR.
  The supplier publishes that IOR only after creating its event channel, so
  slow loaded runners could exceed the default startup interval. Added a
  60-second supplier startup allowance, consistent with other Notify
  performance tests. The test was regenerated, clean-built, syntax-checked,
  and all four scenarios passed locally.

## 2026-11-11 sequence buffer comparison review rule

- Treat IDL `sequence<char>` as a length-delimited byte sequence, not a C
  string: its `get_buffer()` result is not guaranteed to be NUL-terminated.
  Compare `length()` first and then compare exactly that many bytes with
  `std::memcmp`; use `strcmp` only for actual IDL `string` values or buffers
  with guaranteed NUL termination.
- Applied this to the DII collocation oneway and twoway tests after Windows
  reported failures from `strcmp` on unbounded `sequence<char>`. Both projects
  were realclean-built and their six-mode `run_test.pl` harnesses passed.
  Commit `7a55c94d43a` was pushed.
- A repository-wide source search for string comparisons on `get_buffer()` found
  no further `strcmp` misuse. The remaining direct comparisons are bytewise
  `memcmp`, and the bounded DII sequence checks use an explicit bound.

## 2026-11-11 Review lessons from OpenDDS PR 5327

- Compatibility code should centralize API differences in one helper rather than duplicate wrappers across backends. Keep the ACE 6 / C++03 compatibility path syntactically compatible, and make feature macros correspond to the API they actually select; document any deliberate coupling.
- Prefer the native returned type and avoid copies: do not wrap a returned `std::string` in a compatibility conversion, and use const references for repeatedly queried container results when their lifetime permits.
- Treat narrow and wide IDL literals separately (`strval` versus `wstrval`). Never assume they share storage or convert one through the other.
- Check every caller of a changed TAO IDL API, including out-of-diff logging sites. `std::string` must be passed as `c_str()` to ACE variadic logging formats; otherwise GCC may emit garbage and Clang can reject it.
- Verified against PR 5327's review comments and subsequent commits through approved commit `9142c856f6ea0149bf11a8c48b63d031ef64f729`; these checks are now part of the modernization tracker.

## 2026-11-11 Additional OpenDDS PR 5327 review lessons

- Put cross-version accessors for related values next to each other in one shared compatibility header when both backends can include it. Avoid duplicate helper headers in separate generator directories.
- A compatibility gate should describe the API capability it selects. If ownership changes happen to land with a string API change, document that coupling or use a capability-specific gate.
- For string-valued API changes, keep the native `std::string` result when it is already the desired value; do not add a legacy wrapper or compatibility conversion that creates a temporary. Use a `const std::string&` for repeated container results when the source outlives the use.
- Audit all diagnostics and varargs call sites, including unchanged files and functions. A changed string return type can silently break `%C` logging beyond the diff.
- Keep narrow and wide literal values separate at every backend boundary, and test both. `EV_wstring` must read `wstrval`; a narrow value may be empty even when its wide counterpart is populated.
- Keep unrelated behavior and cleanup out of a compatibility/API migration. Review whether every changed line is necessary for the migration, and label pre-existing defects as separate follow-ups.
- Apply API migration consistently at each call site: use the native string type when the new API returns it, and avoid inconsistent local representations without a specific lifetime or ABI reason.
- Validate both compatibility configurations with actual builds. Obtain the required legacy headers/toolchain rather than treating their absence as evidence that the compatibility path builds.
- Explain new API terminology in user-facing documentation and link to its contract/specification; do not assume downstream users know what “modern API” means.
- When porting downstream code to a changed API, distinguish required compatibility shims from unrelated API/behavior edits. For each shim, identify the upstream declaration that requires it. Keep formatting-only suggestions and pre-existing defects out of the migration unless separately requested.

## 2026-11-11 OpenDDS PR 5327 follow-up review findings

- An API migration audit must include unchanged callers, especially every variadic logging boundary. A `std::string` passed as `%C` to `ACE_ERROR` is not a valid C-string argument: GCC may accept it but produce garbage or fail at runtime, and Clang can reject it. Convert explicitly with the compatibility helper at the varargs boundary and search all uses of the changed accessor, not only the diff.
- Validate semantic output for distinct string domains. TAO stores `EV_wstring` in `wstrval`; using `strval` can silently emit an empty wide constant. Audit each backend (including Java and annotations) and add/refresh coverage for wide literals, rather than relying only on a successful compile.
- Keep compatibility logic centralized and shared across consumers. Avoid parallel helper headers in generator subdirectories and repeated inline `#ifdef` mappings. Compatibility wrappers should only bridge APIs that actually differ; when both versions already yield the desired `std::string`, use it directly.
- Avoid unnecessary copies in generated-code paths: return references to long-lived key lists when consumers only read them, and do not wrap a C-string conversion in a temporary `ACE_CString` if the function already returns that value.
- Keep each patch line tied to the stated migration. Reviewers flagged unrelated cleanup mixed into the API port; move pre-existing defects or unrelated edits to a follow-up. Where a feature gate also controls a separate ownership API, either use a gate named for that capability or document why the APIs are guaranteed to arrive together.
- Treat review style suggestions as project-specific. Keep declarations/casts consistent with the target repository’s established formatting, and do not let formatting cleanups obscure the API adaptation.
- Validate the actual legacy and modern configurations. A compatibility path is not verified by inspection or by noting missing local headers; obtain the matching headers/toolchain and build both paths. Also run the generator tests that check emitted narrow and wide values.
- Prefer a `const std::string` local when the new API naturally returns an owned string and the value is used as a string. Use a compatibility C-string accessor only where a legacy API (such as a varargs logger) requires `const char*`; avoid converting back to `ACE_CString` only to return it.
- Avoid per-call copies of containers returned by reference, and keep converted sites consistent about whether they retain strings or expose `c_str()` pointers. Check the lifetime before choosing a reference or pointer.
- When one compatibility header can serve multiple backends, share it rather than maintaining near-identical copies. Put cross-version narrow/wide value accessors there instead of repeating conditional compilation at each use site.
- Exercise behavior-specific paths affected by API changes: wide string literals need a test that proves `wstrval` is populated and consumed, and logging call sites need compiler/runtime checks that catch non-trivial objects crossing varargs.
- Do not infer one feature from another in preprocessor gates. A `std::unique_ptr` return and a `std::string` API may be introduced together, but ownership and string capabilities are distinct; use separate feature tests or document the coupling precisely.

  the root POA and manager factory transfer into local owners and are destroyed
  after the lock is released; the members are not read afterward. Initialization
  creates the manager factory before the root POA on configurations that use
  it, so the factory-null return after root transfer is unreachable in normal
  initialized state.
- No defect or code change was justified. This extends the partial
  `TAO/tao` move review; the repository-wide audit remains open.
